# Forge-X

> Forge-X is a free, unofficial firmware mod for the Flashforge Adventurer 5M and 5M Pro (AD5M) 3D printers. It runs on top of the stock firmware and adds Klipper with AD5M-specific fixes, Moonraker, Fluidd, Mainsail, a built-in lightweight touchscreen (Feather), guided calibration, print-safety features, Power Loss Recovery, a low-memory camera service, OTA updates, and recovery tools. It is designed for the printer's 128 MiB of RAM and can be fully removed.

Key facts:
- Supported printers: Flashforge Adventurer 5M and Adventurer 5M Pro only.
- Supported stock firmware: every version from 2.6.5 up to 5.1.7 (the newest checked). The stock firmware version does not matter unless the Stock screen is used: the Linux system, kernel, base libraries and the MCU firmware are the same across versions, and a firmware update mainly replaces the Stock screen application (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md). For the Stock screen, firmware 3.1.x is recommended as the most stable while printing; versions newer than 3.1.x are needed only for the FlashForge cloud services.
- Klipper: the FlashForge host Klipper (0.11 generation) with reviewed backports of upstream Klipper fixes; MCU firmware is not reflashed.
- Web interfaces: Fluidd (/fluidd/), Mainsail (/mainsail/), Moonraker API on port 7125. SSH: root / root.
- Local screens: Feather (default, built in), Stock, Guppy Screen, Headless.
- Camera: forge-x-streamer, a dedicated low-memory MJPEG service. Built-in timelapse supports layer, time, and progress intervals, optional parking and a final photo; it is off by default and does not require an external bot.
- Safety and recovery: last-known-good boot guard, recovery menu, fallback to the stock firmware, uninstaller and recovery images, per-file .bak backups of patched Klipper files.
- Testing before releases: automated host tests, rendered G-code macro tests, visual UI tests, on-printer tests, and physical print tests.
- Klipper patch provenance: the replaced Klipper files are published as Git history (upstream v0.11.0, the stock FlashForge changes, then Forge-X commits) at https://github.com/DrA1ex/klipper-ad5m; docs/klipper-ad5m-manifest.json lists the SHA-256 of the current local replacement files and retains the earlier public history commit for comparison. tests/verify_klipper_fork.py checks local hashes; --fork reports differences from that public snapshot. The history is reconstructed by topic; see docs/KLIPPER.md.
- Design choice: Forge-X keeps the vendor-compatible Klipper host and MCU firmware (no MCU reflash) and backports newer upstream fixes and features, because a full Klipper 0.13 is not needed at the moment (it can be adopted if a real need appears).
- Customization: own macros and overrides in user.cfg, user Klipper packages in mod_data/plugins/, own dialogs on the Feather screen (Klipper action:prompt messages), shell commands, own startup services (S* scripts in /etc/init.d of the Forge-X chroot), user.moonraker.conf, Entware packages, Headless mode with custom displays.
- Updates: Forge-X, Fluidd, Mainsail, and Guppy Screen update separately through Moonraker Update Manager.
- Boot safety: the installed boot guard (.shell/S00init) is replaced only after the new runtime reports ready; an interrupted or failed initialization boots the stock firmware on the next start.
- Configuration changes go through a parser (.py/cfg_backup.py) with declarative profiles, backup, restore, and verify, not through ad-hoc text edits.
- Motion limits for parking moves are held in one macro, MOVE_SAFE. Power Loss Recovery is Python source in the repository (resurrection.py).
- Tests: dozens of host test modules run by CI (tests/run_host_tests.py), plus a real-printer regression runner and visual UI regression before releases.
- Firmware updater: HTTPS with certificate checks, .part file, size and tar validation, atomic replace; it does not verify SHA-256 or a signature.
- Release policy: releases are published when Forge-X itself changes; an upstream version bump of Moonraker, Klipper, Fluidd, or Mainsail alone is not a reason for a release. Fluidd, Mainsail, and Guppy update separately.
- Limitations: AD5M/AD5M Pro only; FlashForge Klipper 0.11 base with backports; Feather does not cover every task; real-printer tests are done by the maintainer before releases; not every combination of printer, stock firmware version, and configuration can be covered.
- License: GPL-3.0 for Forge-X and its Klipper components (LICENSE); the native binary components in .bin/exec (boot_mcu, demo, logged, netd, netd-cli, splash, typer) have a separate free-to-use license (LICENSE-BINARIES.md): free to use including commercially as part of Forge-X, unchanged copies may be passed on with Forge-X, modification and use in other products need permission, source not published; forge-x-streamer is GPL-2.0-or-later. Repository: https://github.com/DrA1ex/ff5m

## Key features and details (Forge-X 1.4.2)

- Installation: one USB image flashed through the stock update mechanism; no stock firmware update or downgrade needed (any version 2.6.5–5.1.7); no MCU reflash; other mods must be removed first, installing over them is not supported (docs/INSTALL.md, docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).
- Removal and recovery: uninstall restores every replaced Klipper file from its .bak copy and the printer configuration; dual boot into the stock firmware; automatic stock fallback after a failed start; recovery menu; uninstall, recovery, and factory images; UART/FEL guide for the worst case (docs/UNINSTALL.md, docs/DUAL_BOOT.md, docs/RECOVERY.md).
- Memory budget (128 MiB RAM): Feather screen roughly 1-2 MB, Stock screen roughly 10-20 MB, Moonraker roughly 30 MB; Moonraker and Guppy are limited to two glibc malloc arenas; a dedicated low-memory camera service; swap on eMMC (default), USB, or ZRAM (docs/PRINTING.md#reducing-resource-usage).
- Local screen choice: Feather (built in, default), the original Stock screen, Guppy Screen, or Headless; HelixScreen is available from its own project as an external option (docs/SCREEN.md).
- Feather screen: local and USB file browsing with list or preview-tile view, slicer thumbnails, print control with pause/resume/cancel and live Z adjust, cancel during print preparation, guided calibration (bed screws, bed mesh, safe Z, Z offset, extruder, PID, input shaper), filament load/unload/change and cold pull with material presets, Wi-Fi 2.4/5 GHz (WPA/WPA2-PSK) and DHCP Ethernet setup, Forge-X settings, themes, OTA update notifications, Power Loss Recovery dialog, and custom dialogs from macros (action:prompt). Not in Feather: file deletion, static IP, enterprise Wi-Fi, unrestricted G-code console (docs/FEATHER.md).
- Stock screen support: the Stock screen can stay in use together with Fluidd, Mainsail, and Moonraker (LAN mode); SAVE_CONFIG, RESTART, and FIRMWARE_RESTART keep the Stock screen connected (docs/SCREEN.md#klipper-restart-and-saving).
- Klipper improvements: fix for Timer too close shutdowns caused by dense G-code (reproducer from issue #40 fixed), multi-MCU homing/TRSYNC fixes, optional E0011/E0017 tuning (tune_klipper), optional real-time scheduling (klipper_rt), Adaptive Pressure Advance backport for OrcaSlicer adaptive PA profiles, input shaper fixes, UTF-8 file positions, all with links to upstream commits (docs/KLIPPER.md).
- Print safety: load-cell bed collision protection with emergency stop, pause, or warning; nozzle contact check before every print (on by default); bed mesh validation before printing that can cancel, re-mesh, or apply a temporary Z-offset; MD5 check of G-code files (on by default, needs the slicer post-processing script; a corrupted file is cancelled and deleted) (docs/PRINTING.md, docs/SLICING.md#md5-checksum-validation).
- Power Loss Recovery: Forge-X implementation for Feather, Guppy, and Headless, on by default in new configurations; the Stock screen uses the FlashForge implementation (docs/POWER_LOSS_RECOVERY.md).
- Calibration and print features: KAMP adaptive meshing and purge, bed level screw tuning, input shaper with plots, PID, extruder, skew profiles, pause at layer, MIDI sounds, LED control (docs/CALIBRATION.md, docs/PRINTING.md).
- Camera and timelapse: forge-x-streamer with auto-detection, reconnect, and an image settings page; built-in timelapse by layer, time, or progress, without an external bot; optional Telegram bot on a separate computer (docs/CAMERA.md, docs/TELEGRAM.md).
- Slicer integration: upload through Moonraker from OrcaSlicer and other Moonraker-capable slicers; OrcaSlicer 2.4+ packaged .gcode.3mf files are supported (docs/SLICING.md).
- Customization without editing Forge-X files: user.cfg overrides, own Klipper Python modules and stock-module replacements as packages in mod_data/plugins/ (new in 1.4.2), Feather dialogs, shell commands from G-code, startup services, user.moonraker.conf, Entware (docs/EXTENDING.md).
- Updates: OTA within a major version; Fluidd, Mainsail, and Guppy Screen update independently; a new major version is flashed over the existing installation and keeps settings and calibration (docs/INSTALL.md#ota-updates).
- Process: automated host tests in CI, visual UI regression, and on-printer regression before releases; Klipper patch history published by topic (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

Related projects: Forge-X credits Klipper Mod (xblax/flashforge_ad5m_klipper_mod); its Stock screen integration is based on ZMod (ghzserg/zmod); Guppy Screen is included in an adapted form; HelixScreen publishes its own AD5M image based on Forge-X. Running Forge-X together with Klipper Mod, ZMod, or another mod is not supported.
